Could Late Biosimilar Launches Slow Amgen Stock?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Amgen (AMGN) stock returned 59.4% over the past year, against 9.9% for the S&P 500. The shares also cost more per dollar of earnings than the index, suggesting that buyers expect the company’s growth to continue. Part of that expansion comes from biosimilars, which are Amgen’s versions of drugs such as EYLEA, and the company has more of them in development. On a November 3 call, management outlined what it will take for those upcoming launches to succeed. What could go wrong for Amgen’s next biosimilars?

The risk is that Amgen’s next biosimilars reach the market after the first wave of competing products, and it remains too early to know whether they will. During the November 3 call, management said Amgen aims to be first or in the first wave with its biosimilar launches. Executives called this timing “really important to establish a decent competitive position,” adding that management believes Amgen is in that position.

The next four pipeline drugs are versions of EYLEA HD, OPDIVO, KEYTRUDA and OCREVUS, which management called large market opportunities. Because all four are still in late-stage clinical development, an early launch is management’s belief, not a result.

Biosimilars generated $977 million in fiscal Q3 2026, accounting for about 9% of Amgen’s total revenue. While they remain a small part of the company, these sales are growing rapidly. Biosimilar sales rose 26% from a year earlier, compared with an 8% increase for all of Amgen’s product sales. PAVBLU, Amgen’s version of EYLEA, made up $300 million of that total, climbing 41% from a year earlier.

The stock price leaves little room for disappointment. Amgen closed on November 5 just 3.8% below its highest close of the past year. The stock trades at 26.5 times earnings, against 22.9 for the S&P 500.

Amgen stock enters next phase after Q3 growth and outlook lift
sum: Amgen reported stronger third-quarter results on November 3, 2026, and raised its full-year outlook. The company said in a PR Newswire release that revenue increased 8 percent from the year-earlier period to 10.4 billion US dollars.

GAAP earnings per share rose 19 percent to 7.08 US dollars from 5.93 US dollars. Non-GAAP earnings per share increased 14 percent to 6.45 US dollars from 5.64 US dollars. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 47.3 percent, up from 47.1 percent, while free cash flow fell to 3.7 billion US dollars from 4.2 billion US dollars, mainly because of working-capital changes.

Amgen's commercial performance remained uneven across its portfolio. Repatha revenue rose 37 percent to 1.085 billion US dollars, and Evenity sales increased 39 percent to 751 million US dollars. Uplizna revenue jumped 191 percent to 451 million US dollars, while Imdelltra sales advanced 128 percent to 406 million US dollars.

Older products faced sharper pressure from biosimilar competition. Prolia sales declined 45 percent to 632 million US dollars and Xgeva sales dropped 47 percent to 288 million US dollars. The contrasting product trends leave Amgen reliant on newer growth drivers to offset erosion in established medicines.

Amgen raised its 2026 revenue forecast to a range of 38.9 billion to 39.7 billion US dollars, compared with the previous range of 38.2 billion to 39.4 billion US dollars. The company lifted its non-GAAP earnings-per-share outlook to 22.90 to 23.70 US dollars from 22.30 to 23.50 US dollars.

Management expects capital expenditures of approximately 2.6 billion US dollars and share repurchases of no more than 3 billion US dollars. It also expects a full-year non-GAAP operating margin of roughly 45 percent to 46 percent of product sales and said it does not anticipate a step-down in operating margin in 2027 compared with its 2026 guidance.

Chief Executive Robert Bradway said the commercial portfolio, clinical progress and late-stage pipeline support durable growth. The company highlighted continued development of MariTide in obesity, as well as programs involving Repatha, Uplizna, TEZSPIRE and Imdelltra.

Amgen stock in focus as company raises 2026 outlook
sum: Amgen reported third-quarter 2026 results on Tuesday, November 3, after the U.S. market close. In a company release, management said revenue increased 8% year over year to 10.4 billion US dollars, with product sales also up 8%.

Amgen's GAAP earnings per share rose to 7.08 US dollars from 5.93 US dollars in the year-earlier quarter. Adjusted earnings per share increased to 6.45 US dollars from 5.64 US dollars, while adjusted operating income reached 4.7 billion US dollars and the adjusted operating margin was 47.3%.

The result combined lower acquisition-related costs with continued investment in the pipeline. Research and development spending increased 11% to 2.1 billion US dollars. Free cash flow declined to 3.7 billion US dollars from 4.2 billion US dollars, which Amgen attributed mainly to working-capital movements and favorable timing effects in the prior-year quarter.

The product portfolio showed a sharp split between growth medicines and established brands facing biosimilar competition. Repatha sales rose 37% to 1.085 billion US dollars, while EVENITY sales increased 39% to 751 million US dollars. UPLIZNA revenue jumped 191% to 451 million US dollars, and IMDELLTRA sales climbed 128% to 406 million US dollars.

By contrast, Prolia sales fell 45% to 632 million US dollars and XGEVA sales dropped 47% to 288 million US dollars as multiple biosimilars launched globally. Amgen also said Enbrel's net selling price fell 14%, reflecting the ongoing impact of U.S. Medicare Part D price setting under the Inflation Reduction Act.

For 2026, Amgen now expects revenue of 38.9 billion to 39.7 billion US dollars. Adjusted earnings per share are projected at 22.90 to 23.70 US dollars, while GAAP earnings per share are expected in a range of 18.34 to 19.28 US dollars. The company also expects capital expenditure of approximately 2.6 billion US dollars and share repurchases of no more than 3.0 billion US dollars.
Chief Executive Robert Bradway said the commercial portfolio, clinical advances and late-stage pipeline support Amgen's confidence in durable growth.

items.t: Eli Lilly Rises 4% While Foundayo Nears European Approval; Amgen and Novo Nordisk Edge Higher
sum: A European regulatory committee just handed Eli Lilly a potential edge over Novo Nordisk in the obesity pill race, and one key detail about how patients take the drug could tip the competitive balance.

A European regulatory endorsement for an oral obesity pill is lifting Eli Lilly (NYSE:LLY | LLY Price Prediction) stock ahead of the rest of the drug group. Eli Lilly stock is up 4% to $1,295.58 in afternoon trading, with the gain building on a recommendation that brings Foundayo closer to European patients. Foundayo now stands one regulatory step from final approval in the European Union, where a rival oral obesity pill already holds authorization.

Checking in on the peers, Amgen (NASDAQ:AMGN) stock is up 2% to $433.71, a solid gain that still trails Eli Lilly stock by a wide margin. Novo Nordisk (NYSE:NVO) stock is up 2% to $39.17, landing in line with Amgen stock and well behind Eli Lilly stock. Amgen and Novo Nordisk shares are moving in step, leaving Eli Lilly stock as the clear outlier on the upside.

Drug and biotechnology stocks are rising broadly alongside Eli Lilly shares, with the iShares Biotechnology ETF (NASDAQ:IBB) up 2% to $209.12. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.3% to $768.56, a much quieter move that makes today’s healthcare-sector strength stand out against the broader market.
European Endorsement Brings Foundayo Within Reach of Approval

On October 16, the European Medicines Agency’s human medicines committee recommended approval of Foundayo, Eli Lilly’s oral obesity pill, for weight management and for diabetes treatment. That recommendation puts Foundayo on course to become the second oral drug of its class in the European Union. European Commission decisions generally come within a few weeks of such recommendations, giving Lilly a short track to a final ruling.

Novo Nordisk reached European patients first with its Wegovy pill, which is approved there for weight management only, while the committee’s recommendation covers both weight management and diabetes for Foundayo, giving Eli Lilly a wider proposed label in the same oral category. Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk lead the obesity and diabetes drug market, which makes that scale significant.

Is Amgen Stock Worth More Than Its Competitors?
sum: Amgen (AMGN) competes in a tight peer group of six large drugmakers alongside AbbVie, Johnson & Johnson, Merck, Pfizer, and Bristol-Myers Squibb. The company ranks second within this group for both sales growth and operating margin. Its valuation tells a different story. Leaving out Merck and Pfizer, which each reported a loss in at least one of their last four quarters, Amgen has the third highest P/E of the four companies that can be compared. So how far apart are what Amgen delivers and what you pay for it?

Johnson & Johnson provides the clearest point of comparison. Amgen grew its revenue by 9.1% over the past twelve months, beating the 8.1% rate at Johnson & Johnson. Amgen also retained a larger share of its sales as operating profit, posting a margin of 30.0% against Johnson & Johnson’s 26.8%. Yet investors pay just 25.8 times earnings for Amgen, compared to 30.2 times for Johnson & Johnson.

AbbVie is the sole peer to beat Amgen on both growth and margin. That performance comes at a steep premium, with AbbVie trading at 78.8 times earnings. Bristol-Myers Squibb offers the lowest valuation at 12.7 times, but its revenue grew by a modest 3.1%. Merck and Pfizer fall out of the price ranking entirely. Both of those companies reported a loss in at least one of their last four quarters.

Executives point to six key growth drivers for Amgen. The company reported on its fiscal Q2 2026 call, held August 4, 2026, that these six grew 26% from a year earlier. Together they accounted for nearly 70% of product sales in that quarter. Repatha, which lowers LDL cholesterol, saw its sales rise 37% in the quarter.

Two other drugs are pulling the overall numbers in the opposite direction. Combined sales of Prolia and XGEVA fell 33% in the same quarter. Management noted that biosimilar competitors, rival copies of the two drugs, have now launched.

Overall growth at Amgen has slowed. Revenue growth hit 16.4% two years ago and 12.9% a year ago, before slowing again over the latest twelve months. The market price appears to assume this slowdown continues.
Amgen expects 2026 revenue of $38.2 billion to $39.4 billion, according to statements management made on that August call. That guidance represents a raise.

sum: Novartis just handed the entire Lp(a) drug class a failing grade, and Amgen is taking the worst of the punishment despite releasing promising trial results of its own on the very same morning.

A failed cholesterol trial from Novartis (NYSE:NVS | NVS Price Prediction) is dragging the Lp(a) drug class lower and hitting Amgen (NASDAQ:AMGN) harder than any large-cap peer in Tuesday trading. The selloff is unfolding even as Amgen posted a positive Phase 3 readout of its own in small cell lung cancer, an unusual split that captures how brutally the market can price competitor risk in biotech.

Amgen stock is down 10% to $394.38 at midday, interrupting a gain of 23% year to date (YTD) heading into the session. The move carries added weight because Amgen holds the fourth-largest position in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, so today’s decline pressures that index alongside health care specifically.

Meanwhile, Eli Lilly (NYSE:LLY) shares are down 2% to $1,124.77 on read-through concerns about its own Lp(a) program. As for Novartis stock, it’s tumbling 14% to $137.63 on Tuesday afternoon. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.37%, so today’s pharma-sector pain isn’t washing across the broad tape. That gap between the biotech names and the benchmark tells you the market is pricing pipeline risk at the sector level.

Novartis said last Thursday that pelacarsen, an experimental heart drug developed with Ionis Pharmaceuticals, failed to reduce cardiovascular risk in a late-stage trial. The Novartis 8,323-patient Phase III study lowered Lp(a) levels while missing its primary composite endpoint covering cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack, non-fatal stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization.

Citi analysts said the Lp(a) hypothesis has been weakened, with additional data needed to establish whether the shortfall came from the drug’s mechanism, the trial’s design, or the underlying idea that lowering Lp(a) reduces cardiovascular risk. Amgen and Eli Lilly are both developing Lp(a)-lowering therapies using different technical approaches, so a class-defining failure at a rival forces investors to reweight the odds on every remaining program.

Amgen Shares Fall as Novartis' Pelacarsen Misses Phase III Study Goal
sum: Shares of Amgen AMGN were down 5% in after-hours trading on Friday after Novartis NVS announced that the phase III Lp(a)HORIZON study evaluating the latter's investigational drug pelacarsen in patients with elevated lipoprotein (a) Lp(a) and established cardiovascular disease (CVD) did not meet its primary endpoint.
Year to date, shares of Amgen have rallied 36.3% compared with the industry's rise of 11.1%.

The double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III Lp(a)HORIZON study is a cardiovascular outcomes study that assessed whether pelacarsen can reduce the incidence of four-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in 8,323 patients with elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] levels and established cardiovascular disease.
Per Novartis, the study failed to meet its primary endpoint of reducing the risk of cardiovascular events compared with placebo in patients with elevated Lp(a) and established cardiovascular disease.

Treatment with pelacarsen substantially lowered Lp(a) levels, consistent with previous studies. However, this reduction did not translate into a lower risk of cardiovascular events in the overall study population. The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke and urgent coronary revascularization requiring hospitalization.
Novartis secured global rights from Ionis Pharmaceuticals IONS to develop, manufacture and commercialize pelacarsen under a licensing and collaboration agreement.
Shares of Novartis and Ionis declined following the announcement of the news on Friday.

Amgen or Biogen: Which Biotech Stock Appears Better Poised?
sum: Biogen BIIB and Amgen AMGN are two of the biggest biotech companies in the world.

Amgen has a strong presence in the oncology, general medicine, inflammation and rare diseases markets. Biogen is making therapies for treating serious neurological, neurodegenerative and rare diseases. Its portfolio spans multiple therapy areas, including multiple sclerosis (MD), Alzheimer's disease, spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), depression, lupus and rare neuromuscular disorders.

Both companies possess extensive and promising pipelines that have the potential to drive innovation and support long-term expansion. The main question for investors, however, is which stock currently presents the more attractive investment opportunity.
Below, we compare their fundamentals, growth outlook and key risks to assess the better pick.

Biogen is in the midst of a major portfolio transition. The company is seeing declining sales of its key MS drugs like Tecfidera and Tysabri, and SMA treatment, Spinraza, due to generic erosion, increasing competition from newer therapies and pricing headwinds.

Amid declining demand for MS drugs and Spinraza, Biogen believes its new products, Eisai-partnered Leqembi for Alzheimer's disease, Skyclarys for Friedreich's ataxia, Qalsody for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and Supernus Pharmaceuticals-partnered Zurzuvae for depression, have the potential to revive growth.

Biogen's growth products (Skyclarys, Qalsody, Zurzuvae, Vumerity and Spinraza plus Alzheimer's revenues from the Leqembi collaboration) generated sales of $851 million in the first quarter, up 12% year over year.
